title: Hoe is hij, hoe is zij?
summary: Describing looks and personality — aardig, gezellig, druk, rustig, grappig, streng

blocks.title: What someone looks like
blocks.body: The outside: *lang* (tall), *klein* (short), *donker haar* (dark hair), *blond haar* (blonde hair), *draagt een bril* (wears glasses).
blocks.callout: *klein* still means 'small' — for a person, it just means 'short'.

blocks.title: What someone is like
blocks.body: The inside: *aardig* (kind, nice), *gezellig* (fun to be around — yes, people can be gezellig too, not just cafés), *druk* (busy, or hyper), *rustig* (calm, quiet), *grappig* (funny), *streng* (strict).

pairs.left: Ik heb het druk — I'm busy (schedule)
pairs.right: Hij is een beetje druk — He's a bit hyper (personality)
pairs.note: Same word, two senses — busy schedule vs. a hyper personality. Context tells you which.

blocks.explain: streng — strict. aardig is kind, grappig is funny.

blocks.scene: Emma describes Daan to you at the café.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.target: Daan? Hij is heel grappig, hoor.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.target: Best druk — altijd praten, praten, praten.
lines.en: Pretty hyper — always talk, talk, talk.
lines.spotlight: druk — here it means hyper, not 'busy with work'.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.target: Heel aardig, ja. Een beetje streng over muziek, maar verder heel gezellig.
lines.en: Very kind, yes. A bit strict about music, but otherwise really fun to be around.

questions.q: What does 'druk' mean in Emma's description of Daan?
